mcqs.question: Inertia is best defined as:

options.A: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion
options.B: The amount of matter contained in a body
options.C: The force exerted by a body due to gravity
options.D: The product of mass and velocity

mcqs.answer: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the property of matter that makes it resist changes in its state of motion. It is not the same as mass (amount of matter) or weight (gravitational force). Option A correctly captures the definition, while the other options describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates the inertia of rest?

options.A: A book lying on a table remains unmoved until someone pushes it.
options.B: A car moving at constant speed continues to move without any force.
options.C: A spinning top keeps rotating after being released.
options.D: A stone falls freely under gravity.

mcqs.answer: A book lying on a table remains unmoved until someone pushes it.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest refers to an object staying at rest unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force. Option A describes exactly this. Options B and C involve motion, and D involves a gravitational force causing motion.

mcqs.question: Which example best demonstrates the inertia of motion?

options.A: A hockey puck sliding on a friction‑less ice surface continues to move in a straight line.
options.B: A ball placed on a shelf stays at rest until nudged.
options.C: A pendulum hanging still at its lowest point.
options.D: A stone being lifted upward by a crane.

mcqs.answer: A hockey puck sliding on a friction‑less ice surface continues to move in a straight line.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion is the tendency of a moving object to keep moving with the same speed and direction unless a net external force acts on it. The puck on frictionless ice experiences negligible external forces, so it maintains its motion, matching option A. The other options involve objects at rest or external forces causing motion.

mcqs.question: A car is traveling straight on a highway. Which scenario best illustrates the inertia of direction?

options.A: The car continues moving straight unless the driver turns the steering wheel.
options.B: The car speeds up when the driver presses the accelerator.
options.C: The car slows down when the brakes are applied.
options.D: The car moves downhill due to gravity.

mcqs.answer: The car continues moving straight unless the driver turns the steering wheel.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction means an object in motion will keep moving in the same straight line unless acted upon by a force that changes its direction. Steering provides that force. Options B, C, and D involve changes in speed or external forces unrelated to direction.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly expresses Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues to move with constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.B: A constant force is required to keep an object moving at constant speed.
options.C: Inertia is the same as weight.
options.D: Force is needed only to start the motion of an object.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues to move with constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law (law of inertia) states exactly what is written in option A. Options B, C, and D are common misconceptions: a constant force is needed only to change motion, inertia differs from weight, and no force is needed to maintain uniform motion.

mcqs.question: Which everyday observation is a direct application of Newton's first law?

options.A: A passenger lurches forward when a moving bus suddenly stops.
options.B: A ball thrown upward returns to the hand.

mcqs.answer: A passenger lurches forward when a moving bus suddenly stops.
mcqs.explanation: When the bus stops, the passenger's body tends to continue moving forward due to inertia, illustrating Newton's first law. The other options involve gravity, magnetic force, and phototropism, which are unrelated to the law of inertia.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes inertia from mass?

options.A: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist changes in its motion, while mass quantifies the amount of matter in the body.
options.B: Inertia is the gravitational force acting on a body, whereas mass is its resistance to acceleration.
options.C: Inertia and mass are identical; both measure weight.
options.D: Inertia applies only to moving objects, while mass applies only to stationary objects.

mcqs.answer: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist changes in its motion, while mass quantifies the amount of matter in the body.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia describes resistance to any change in motion and is directly proportional to mass, but they are not the same. Mass is a measure of the quantity of matter. Options B, C, and D contain incorrect definitions or misconceptions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the inertia of rest is true?

options.A: A heavier object possesses greater inertia of rest than a lighter object.
options.B: Inertia of rest depends only on the shape of the object.
options.C: Inertia of rest becomes zero in a vacuum.
options.D: All objects, regardless of mass, have the same inertia of rest.

mcqs.answer: A heavier object possesses greater inertia of rest than a lighter object.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest is directly proportional to mass; a more massive (heavier) object resists changes to its state of rest more than a less massive one. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because shape alone does not determine inertia, vacuum does not affect inertia, and inertia varies with mass.
